messages:
maria-kwon: FYI getting multiple reports from two APAC customers that requests pinned to eu-central are routing to us-west and showing lots of 500s + p50 spikes. Console shows region marked unhealthy and failover happened around 07:12 UTC. :rotating_light:
jonathan: can you paste a repro curl and any x-headers from the request?
maria-kwon: repro: ```curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"X-Redwood-Region: eu-central\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'```
maria-kwon: sample response headers: ``X-Redwood-Routed-Region: us-west``, ``X-Redwood-Route-Policy: fallback``, status 500, body: "upstream timeout"
kevin-r: seeing same in logs for tenant acme-inc. Heartbeat from eu-central probe shows 2/3 failures around 07:10-07:13. But infra metrics show node CPU and GPU normal.
ashley: ops-bot posted an alert: "region-heartbeat: eu-central healthscore dropped below 0.65 due to probe timeouts" (alert id hb-2026-07-11-41)
ops-bot: [ALERT] region-heartbeat eu-central degraded -> triggered failover to us-west for route default.
jonathan: any recent changes to probe TTLs or firewall rules in eu?
maria-kwon: no config changes on customer side. We did push a small probe agent update 07:05 that tightened the probe timeout from 1.2s -> 900ms for faster detection.
kevin-r: that sounds likely — if real latency is 1s transient, the tighter timeout would flip health to unhealthy (false positive) and cause cross-region reroute + egress.
ashley: customers seeing higher cost due to inter-region traffic, and also some requests erroring because the model variant in us-west is a smaller fallback that returns 500 for certain payloads.
jonathan: can we temporarily revert probe timeout? Who owns probe-agent release? @kevin-r
kevin-r: I can roll back the probe-agent 07:05 release on eu-central right now and bump timeout back to 1.2s. Will coordinate with eng-ml.
maria-kwon: please do. Also need to mark eu-central as healthy manually in console to stop ongoing failover for pinned customers.
ops-bot: action scheduled: rollback probe-agent eu-central -> initiating at 07:28 UTC.
jonathan: for customer escalation thread: list impacted tenants, timeline, per-tenant headers, and whether any billing egress occurred. @maria-kwon can you collect and paste?
maria-kwon: collecting list now (ACME, bluebird, holoai). Confirmed ~3.2k tokens routed inter-region for ACME between 07:12-07:22.
kevin-r: rollback complete at 07:31 UTC. I also increased probe timeout to 1.2s and added a 2s grace window for transient spikes.
ops-bot: [INFO] region-heartbeat eu-central recovered at 07:33 UTC (healthscore 0.92). Routing resumed to eu-central for pinned routes.
ashley: QA: can we add a safeguard so small probe timeout changes don't cause immediate failover? Maybe require two consecutive scoring windows or correlate with backend error rates before failing region.
jonathan: good idea — create an RFC and temporary mitigation to change failover policy to require 2 windows. I'll open follow-up with eng-sre.
maria-kwon: sent customers an update and apology, noting we rolled back probe change and actions taken. They're asking for a postmortem and whether billing will be credited.
kevin-r: assign to eng-sre and support for postmortem and billing review. I'll attach the probe-agent change diff and the rollback commands: ```kubectl -n redwood-probes set image ds/probe-agent=probe-agent:2026-07-11-03 && kubectl rollout restart ds/probe-agent -n redwood-probes```
jonathan: thanks. For now, marking thread resolved once billing outreach is confirmed. :white_check_mark:
